section_summary: This section records the settlement of foreign perpetual leaseholds in Japan through tax exemptions and exchanges of diplomatic notes. It includes Tokyo prefectural and municipal regulations, U.S. Embassy reports, and British, French, and Italian published texts setting April 1942 for conversion of leaseholds to ownership. The final page of the Italian gazette contains unrelated mining notices.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Prefectural regulation on tax exemptions following cancellation of perpetual leases
subfiles.about: Temporarily exempts newly owned former perpetual leasehold land and its buildings from specified prefectural taxes.
subfiles.summary: Prefectural land, property income, and house tax exemptions take effect upon promulgation.

subfiles.title: Tokyo municipal regulation on tax exemptions following cancellation of perpetual leases
subfiles.about: Temporarily exempts newly owned former perpetual leasehold land from the municipal additional land tax.
subfiles.summary: The municipal exemption takes effect upon promulgation; page 155 contains only illegible OCR fragments.

subfiles.title: Perpetual Leaseholds
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports French and Swiss settlements and anticipated settlements with four other countries.
subfiles.summary: Japan exchanged notes with France and Switzerland on April 15, reportedly matching the March 25 British and American agreements. Notes with Italy, the Netherlands, Denmark, and Portugal were under Privy Council consideration.

subfiles.title: British Treaty Series No. 29 (1937)
subfiles.from: Herschel V. Johnson, American Embassy, London
subfiles.about: Forwards five copies of the British White Paper on the March 25 Anglo-Japanese perpetual lease agreement.
subfiles.summary: Johnson sends the White Paper for the Treaty Division.

subfiles.title: Exchange of Notes regarding the Termination of Perpetual Leases in Japan
subfiles.doc_type: published treaty text and exchange of notes
subfiles.from: Robert H. Clive and Naotake Satō
subfiles.to: Naotake Satō and Robert H. Clive
subfiles.about: Sets the terms for ending British perpetual leaseholds in Japan on April 1, 1942.
subfiles.summary: The British note and Japanese reply provide for conversion to ownership without compensation or registration tax on April 1, 1942. Existing tax exemptions continue through March 31, 1942, and Japan waives outstanding disputed taxes. The publication includes Japanese text and an English translation of the reply.

subfiles.title: Transmission of U.S.–Japan Arrangement concerning Perpetual Leaseholds
subfiles.from: For the U.S. Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Donald F. Bigelow, American Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Bern
subfiles.about: Sends copies of the March 25 U.S.–Japan arrangement for League of Nations registration and publication.
subfiles.summary: Requests transmission of one certified and two uncertified copies to the League Secretariat.

subfiles.title: Franco-Japanese Agreement for the Abolition of System of Perpetual Leases in Japan
subfiles.from: Edwin C. Wilson, American Embassy, Paris
subfiles.about: Transmits published French-Japanese notes and summarizes their lease conversion and tax provisions.
subfiles.summary: The agreement ends French perpetual leases on April 1, 1942. Tax exemptions continue through March 31, 1942, and provisions also cover leases sold before conversion.

subfiles.title: French-Japanese correspondence on abolition of perpetual leases
subfiles.about: Publishes the French and Japanese notes agreeing to convert perpetual leases and maintain tax protections.
subfiles.summary: Notes specify April 1942 conversion, continued exemptions, and treatment of transferred French leases; the text continues beyond the reproduced page.

subfiles.title: Abolition of Perpetual Leases in Japan
subfiles.from: Edward L. Reed, American Embassy, Rome
subfiles.about: Transmits the Italian official gazette containing the April 30 Italian-Japanese exchange of notes.
subfiles.summary: Reed supplies treaty reporting details: the exchange took effect April 30, 1937, required no ratification, and preserves tax exemptions until the lease system ends in 1942.

subfiles.title: Gazzetta Ufficiale del Regno d'Italia, No. 235
subfiles.about: Publishes the Italian-Japanese perpetual lease notes alongside unrelated Italian mining concession notices.
subfiles.summary: The April 30 notes end Italian perpetual leases in 1942, convert them to ownership without compensation or registration tax, preserve tax protections, and address leases sold before conversion. The remainder of the extract lists Italian mining and mineral water concessions.
